corrections.before: The code that runs when an object is created and sets up its initial state. In Python it is __init__ (with __new__ doing the allocation); in Java it is a method named after the class.
corrections.after: The object-creation operation that selects an instance and sets up its initial state. In Python, __new__ creates or selects the instance and __init__ initialises it when appropriate; in Java, a constructor is a special declaration named after the class, distinct from an ordinary method.

corrections.before: The Python special method that allocates a new instance before __init__ sets it up. Overriding it to always return the same object is one way to force a singleton.
corrections.after: The Python special method called to create or select an instance, before __init__ initialises it when appropriate. It can return an existing instance; overriding it is one way to implement a singleton.

corrections.before: A copy of an object that duplicates only the outer container; the items inside are shared with the original. Changing a nested list through the copy changes it in the original too.
corrections.after: For a compound object such as a list or dictionary, a copy with a new outer container whose contained objects are shared with the original. Mutating a shared nested list through either container affects that same list; some immutable objects may be returned unchanged by copy.copy.

corrections.before: The operations and behavioural contract an object exposes to callers, including names, accepted arguments, results and expected effects. Java provides interface declarations; Python commonly uses duck typing, abstract base classes or typing.Protocol, with behaviour still needing to meet the caller’s expectations.
corrections.after: The operations and behavioural contract an object exposes to callers, including names, accepted arguments, results and expected effects. Java provides interface declarations; Python commonly uses duck typing, abstract base classes or typing.Protocol, with behaviour still needing to meet the caller’s expectations.

corrections.before: Using an object according to the operations and behaviour it provides rather than requiring membership of a particular declared class. Matching method names alone is insufficient: argument meanings, results and error behaviour must fit the caller’s contract.
corrections.after: Using an object according to the operations and behaviour it provides rather than requiring membership of a particular declared class. Matching method names alone is insufficient: argument meanings, results and error behaviour must fit the caller’s contract.

corrections.before: A GoF structural pattern: a wrapper with the same interface as the object it wraps, which adds behaviour before or after forwarding calls. Wrappers can wrap wrappers, so behaviours stack in any order. Not the same thing as Python's @decorator syntax.
corrections.after: A GoF structural pattern: a wrapper with the same relevant interface as the object it wraps, adding behaviour before or after forwarding calls. Compatible wrappers can wrap other wrappers, but their order may change results. Python’s @decorator syntax is broader than this object pattern.

corrections.before: The standard that gives every character in every writing system a number (a code point). UTF-8 is the usual way to store it as bytes.
corrections.after: A standard assigning code points and properties to encoded characters from many writing systems, along with symbols and other text elements. It does not encode every conceivable character; UTF-8 is one encoding of Unicode text as bytes.

corrections.before: A Python function that returns a single shared (interned) copy of a string, so equal strings can be compared and stored as one object.
corrections.after: A Python function returning a canonical interned string for a value. Keep and use the returned reference: interning does not rewrite other references, and the API does not guarantee interned strings remain alive forever.

corrections.before: A server that receives messages from producers and holds them in queues or topics until consumers take them, such as RabbitMQ, Redis or Kafka.
corrections.after: A service that receives and routes messages between producers and consumers using queues, topics or similar channels. Delivery and retention vary: a queue may remove an acknowledged message, whereas a Kafka topic can retain records after they have been consumed.

corrections.before: A table listing, for each (state, event) pair, the next state. Missing pairs are illegal transitions, and the whole state machine is visible in one place.
corrections.after: A table mapping a state and an event to a next state, making transition rules visible together. In this module’s partial table, a missing pair is treated as an illegal transition; other designs may specify a default or an explicit error transition.

corrections.before: An object that runs a query and hands back result rows, often in batches. Server-side cursors keep the results on the database server and fetch them gradually.
corrections.after: An object that executes a query and provides access to its result rows, often through fetch operations or iteration. A server-side cursor keeps query or traversal state on the database server and lets the client fetch batches rather than receiving the full result at once.

corrections.before: The C++ Standard Template Library of containers and algorithms, which work on any container through iterators.
corrections.after: The C++ Standard Template Library of containers, iterators and algorithms. Iterator-based algorithms can work with different containers when their iterators and elements meet the algorithm’s requirements; not every algorithm accepts every container.

corrections.before: The compiler stage that turns the checked, optimised program representation into machine code or bytecode.
corrections.after: A compiler stage that translates a program representation into a target form, such as machine code, assembly, bytecode or another source language. Required checking and optimisation stages depend on the compiler.

corrections.before: Data before encryption (or after decryption), in its readable form.
corrections.after: Data in its unencrypted form, before encryption or after decryption. It may be text or binary data; the term does not require it to be readable language.

corrections.before: A small immutable object defined by its value rather than its identity, such as Money(10.00, "GBP"), which keeps the rules for that value in one place.
corrections.after: An object identified by its value rather than a separate identity, such as Money(10.00, "GBP"). Value objects are commonly immutable so a value can be shared without unexpected mutation, and they can keep validation and operations for that value together.

corrections.before: A Python standard-library module for network servers. Its request handler calls setup(), handle() and finish(); you override handle().
corrections.after: A Python standard-library module for network servers. After successful setup(), BaseRequestHandler calls handle() and guarantees finish() through finally; if setup() raises, finish() is not called. Subclasses override handle().

corrections.before: Python's built-in testing framework. A TestCase subclass's setUp, test_* and tearDown methods are called by the framework's run(): a template method.
corrections.after: Python’s standard-library testing framework. TestCase.run normally calls setUp, the test method and tearDown in order, a template-method structure; if setUp fails, the test and tearDown are skipped, while registered cleanups have separate guarantees.

An iterable collection’s __iter__ returns a fresh iterator; the iterator protocol’s self-return rule applies to the iterator itself, so the generic method aliases were misleading.

after.definition: The method iter(obj) normally calls to obtain an iterator. A re-iterable collection can return a fresh iterator each time; an iterator’s own __iter__ returns that iterator itself. The older indexed-sequence fallback also allows some objects without __iter__ to be iterable.

corrections.reason: Provide a precise beginner definition for the actual concept.

after.definition: An iterator method called by next(iterator) to produce the next item or raise StopIteration when exhausted. A compliant exhausted iterator keeps raising StopIteration on later calls.

corrections.reason: Provide a precise beginner definition for the actual concept.

after.definition: Spring’s inversion-of-control container creates, configures and assembles application objects called beans. Singleton scope means one bean instance per bean definition per container; it does not imply one global object across independent containers.

gaps: The original selected catalogue remains: chain of responsibility, interpreter, mediator and memento are introduced, without new standalone implementations.

No production Qt/Java UI, Spring deployment, Celery broker, remote payment/cloud effect or production server database was deployed. Exact Python fences, real Django 5.2.18/SQLite, and documented API semantics were checked; illustrative fixtures do not prove omitted business operations.
Several naturally small named-pattern units are below 400 words; they keep coherent boundaries, realistic three-minute study targets and focused questions.
Library API statements are tied to fetched documentation; PBKDF2’s million iterations is explicitly Django 5.2-specific and CPython integer caching is explicitly an implementation detail.
